test_title: PYST 41: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct option with respect to the following statements.

Statement-1: Suspension is a homogeneous mixture.

Statement-2: The particles of a suspension can be seen by the naked eye.

Statement-3: The solute particles settle down when a suspension is left undisturbed, that is, a suspension is unstable.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement 2 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1** claims that a **suspension** is a **homogeneous mixture**. In reality, a **suspension** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the **solute particles** do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the bulk of the medium. In a **homogeneous mixture**, such as a **true solution**, the composition is uniform throughout. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2** mentions that the particles of a **suspension** can be seen by the **naked eye**. This is due to the relatively large size of the particles, which are typically larger than **1000 nanometers** (or **1 micrometer**) in diameter. Unlike **colloids** or **true solutions**, where particles are too small to be seen without magnification, **suspension particles** are large enough to scatter **visible light**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3** states that the **solute particles** settle down when a **suspension** is left **undisturbed**, meaning the **suspension** is **unstable**. Because the particles are large and heavy, the force of **gravity** eventually overcomes the kinetic energy keeping them dispersed, leading to **sedimentation**. Once the particles settle at the bottom, the mixture no longer scatters light as effectively. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **physical state** of a **suspension** can be altered through **filtration**. Since the particles are larger than the pores of **filter paper**, they can be easily separated from the **solvent** or **dispersion medium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of Suspensions:**

 
 
• A **suspension** is **heterogeneous** in nature, meaning its components are not distributed uniformly.
 
• The particles scatter a **beam of light** passing through it and make its path **visible**; this phenomenon is known as the **Tyndall Effect**. However, the **Tyndall Effect** disappears once the particles have settled down.
 
• **Examples** of suspensions include **muddy water**, **chalk powder in water**, **flour in water**, and **milk of magnesia**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Mixtures:**
 
 
• **True Solution:** It is a **homogeneous mixture** with a particle size less than **1 nm**. These particles do not scatter light and cannot be seen by the **naked eye**. They are highly **stable** and do not settle.
 
• **Colloid:** It is a **heterogeneous mixture** that appears **homogeneous**. Particle sizes range between **1 nm and 1000 nm**. They show the **Tyndall Effect** but do not settle down, making them **stable**.
 
 
 
• **Applications and Facts:**
 
 
• In the **pharmaceutical industry**, many medicines are prepared as **suspensions** (e.g., antacids) and must be shaken well before **use** to redistribute the settled **solute particles**.
 
• The **instability** of a **suspension** is a key characteristic used in **water treatment plants**, where **coagulants** are added to help suspended impurities settle faster through **sedimentation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Particle Size:** The defining **feature** of a **suspension** is a particle size greater than **10^-6 meters**.
 
• **Separation:** Unlike **colloids**, which require **centrifugation**, **suspensions** can be separated by simple **mechanical filtration**.
 
• **Optical Properties:** An active **suspension** is **opaque** or **translucent**, but the **supernatant liquid** may become **transparent** once the particles settle.
